Forecast and alert sources

Every outside service El Nino Watch uses to forecast rain and river flow, to raise alerts, and to check those alerts against what has been observed in Somalia.

Each entry says what the app uses it for.

← Back to El Nino Watch Download PDF (English) Privacy notice ↓ Checked against the app on 15 October 2026.
Official national source: Somali National Hydrological Services (MOEWR)

The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources publishes the national flood forecast the app shows as official alerts. ICPAC's regional forecasts, Google Flood Hub's river forecasts and GDACS event monitoring are not official warnings, and the app labels them that way.

Forecasts

5 sources
  • Open-Meteo Weather Forecast APIOpen-Meteo

    Daily and hourly rainfall forecasts for all 30 cities. The app's server fetches them once and shares them with every visitor. These are computer model estimates, not station measurements.

    • Abouthttps://open-meteo.com/en/docs
    • APIhttps://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast
  • Open-Meteo Flood APIGloFAS river discharge, via Open-Meteo

    River discharge forecast for each city.

    • Abouthttps://open-meteo.com/en/docs/flood-api
    • APIhttps://flood-api.open-meteo.com/v1/flood
  • ICPAC Weekly Exceptional Rainfall ForecastAlso alertsIGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre

    Heavy, very heavy and extremely heavy rainfall forecasts for the week (above the 90th, 95th and 99th percentiles for that week of the year). Drives the Alerts tab and the rainfall layers on the flood map.

    • Abouthttps://www.icpac.net/weekly-forecast/
    • Portalhttps://eahazardswatch.icpac.net/
    • Datahttps://eahazardswatch.icpac.net/api/datasets/
    • Map layershttps://eahazardswatch.icpac.net/mapserver/
  • ENSO Diagnostic DiscussionNOAA Climate Prediction Center

    The current El Niño status and outlook.

    • Abouthttps://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso_advisory/ensodisc.shtml
  • Weekly Niño sea-surface temperature indexNOAA Climate Prediction Center

    Weekly El Niño ocean temperatures.

    • Datahttps://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/data/indices/wksst9120.for

The app also links to meteoblue's Galkayo forecast for comparison. It does not use meteoblue's data.

  • Comparehttps://www.meteoblue.com/en/weather/today/gaalkacyo_somalia_59611

Alerts and event monitoring

4 sources
  • Somali National Hydrological ServicesOfficialMinistry of Energy and Water Resources (MOEWR)

    The official national flood forecast: each region's daily flood level (advisory, watch or warning) for the active rainy season, with anticipatory-action pre-activation and activation. Shown as official alerts for the cities in each region.

    • Portalhttps://hydro.tekhub.so/
  • Google Flood HubGoogle Research · Flood Forecasting API

    River flood forecasts at river gauges, from Google's AI model. A gauge forecast at Flood Hub's Warning, Danger or Extreme level within 25 km of a monitored city becomes an alert for that city. A model forecast, not an official warning. Used once Google approves the app's access to the API; the data is under the CC BY 4.0 licence.

    • Portalhttps://sites.research.google/floods/
    • APIhttps://floodforecasting.googleapis.com/v1/
    • Guidehttps://developers.google.com/flood-forecasting
  • GDACSGlobal Disaster Alert and Coordination System

    Flood and other disaster events affecting Somalia, shown as event monitoring.

    • Abouthttps://www.gdacs.org/
    • APIhttps://www.gdacs.org/gdacsapi/api/events/geteventlist/SEARCH
    • Guidehttps://gdacs.org/Documents/2025/GDACS_API_quickstart_v1.pdf
  • ICPAC Weekly Exceptional Rainfall ForecastListed under Forecasts

    Rainfall alerts for each city, from the forecast above.

    • Portalhttps://eahazardswatch.icpac.net/

Observations that support the alerts

5 sources

What has actually been measured or seen from satellites, used to check forecasts and alerts against conditions on the ground.

  • SWALIM river stationsFAO Somalia Water and Land Information Management

    • Stationshttps://snrfa.faoswalim.org/stations/

  • Global Flood Monitoring (GFM)Copernicus Emergency Management Service

Privacy

What El Nino Watch keeps about you, and who else sees what. There are no accounts, no cookies and no advertising, and nothing is sold.

  • Visit counts

    Each page load is counted, with the tab, city, language, type of device and the country the connection comes from. No cookies, internet addresses or browser details are stored, and browsers that ask not to be tracked are not counted. The totals are shown on the visitor statistics page.

  • Community reports

    Reports and comments are public: what you write, the name or alias you give (or Anonymous), any location you add, and photos or videos exactly as uploaded, which may contain location data. Your internet address is held in memory for up to 10 minutes to limit abuse, and is never saved. Only the browser that sent a report can delete it, using a receipt kept in that browser.

  • WhatsApp alerts

    If you sign up, your WhatsApp number, the cities you follow and your language are kept only to send the alerts. Messages go through Meta's WhatsApp service. Replying STOP deletes them.

  • Saved in your browser

    Your language, home city, added cities, report receipts, alerts already shown, city manager review stages and private notes are saved in your own browser, not sent to El Nino Watch. Clearing the site's data in your browser removes them.

  • Other services

    Forecasts, alerts and news are fetched by the El Nino Watch server, so those services do not see you. The flood map's layers and the place-name search for added cities load directly from their publishers, who see your internet address as any website does. Share buttons contact X or Facebook only when you tap them. The site is hosted on bunny.net, which handles every request as any web host does.

Questions about privacy: contact@mandekconsulting.com

Not listed: the base map and elevation services (Natural Earth, Esri World Imagery, Open-Meteo Elevation and place-name search), which draw the map but do not forecast or alert.

Community reports in the app come from residents and are unverified.
